verdicts.claim: The dedicated 8-card 'displacement' probe section returned an identical answer ("no") on 8/8 cards, with notes filled in on only 1 of 8 — and on that 8th card Austin ex
verdicts.reason: The counting half holds: all 8 card_ids exist, all 8 answers are displacement:["no"], exactly 1 of 8 (COIN_2026-07-24) carries a note, and the quote is byte-verbatim. But the load-bearing diagnosis — 'no contrast/yes cases were ever shown, so it never tested whether he CAN recognize displacement' — is false on three independent checks. (1) The committed builder research/g82_master_homework.py::pick_displacement draws from DISP_BUCKETS = tiny(want 2), boundary(3), clear(1), big(2); the wants sum to exactly 8 and exactly 8 cards were emitted, so every bucket filled — 3 of the 8 charts had separation >= 1.25 ATR (1 'clear', 2 'big'). Contrast cases WERE shown by construction; the section was explicitly built to straddle the boundary. (2) The card offers three chips YES / NO / CAN'T TELL and probe_page.question renders every chip aria-pressed="false" with no default, so 8 'no' answers are 8 deliberate presses, not an untouched field. (3) On COIN_2026-07-24 he identifies displacement on that very chart ('displaced and closed into the levels at 9:45') — inside the section he demonstrably recognizes the thing. The correct reading is the opposite of the claim: his eye rejected 3 charts the separation metric scored as displaced, which is a finding about the metric. Accepting this claim would discard 8 real judgements as instrument noise — the exact harm the no-oversell rule exists to prevent. Note also his 'you cant remember what it means' addresses us/the engine, not the deck's composition.
verdicts.recomputed_support: 8/8 'no' and 1/8 notes CONFIRMED as claimed; but n_relevant=8 conceals that the 8 were bucketed 2 tiny / 3 boundary / 1 clear / 2 big by separation_atr, i.e. 3 designed contrast cases.
